questions.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals.

| $f(x,y)$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ | $…$ |
| $X=1$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ | $…$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.3$ | $0.25$ | $0.45$ | $1$ |

Therefore, the probability mass function for  $Y$ is given by the following table:

| $y$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.3$ | $0.25$ | $0.45$ |

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\  & =0\cdot 0.3+1\cdot 0.25+2\cdot 0.45 \\  & =0+0.25+0.9 \\  & =1.15.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}y, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{3}{4},$ find $\text{E}[4X+6Y].$
questions.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[X].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[Y].$

The marginal density function for $Y$ when $0\le y\le 2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}y[{x}^{3}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}y({1}^{3}-0) \\  & =\frac{y}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }y\,{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y\cdot \frac{y}{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[{y}^{3}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(8-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4X+6Y] & =4\,\text{E}[X]+6\,\text{E}[Y] \\  & =4(\frac{3}{4})+6(\frac{4}{3}) \\  & =3+8 \\  & =11.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{9}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3}), & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{23}{15},$ find $\text{E}[3X-Y].$
questions.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[Y].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[X].$

The marginal density function for $X$ when $0\le x\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{2}{9}({x}^{3}+{y}^{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2}{9}{[{x}^{3}y+\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}(2{x}^{3}+\frac{{2}^{4}}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{9}({x}^{3}+2).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot \frac{4}{9}({x}^{3}+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{9}{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{4}+2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{4}{9}{[\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{4}{9}(\frac{1}{5}+1-0) \\  & =\frac{8}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[3X-Y] & =3\,\text{E}[X]+(-1)\,\text{E}[Y] \\  & =3\,(\frac{8}{15})-(\frac{23}{15}) \\  & =\frac{1}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the joint probability distribution for two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ below, find $\text{E}[Y].$

| $f$ | $Y=-2$ | $Y=-1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.25$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the marginal distribution for $X$ corresponds to the row totals, and the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals.

| $f(x,y)$ | $Y=-2$ | $Y=-1$ | ${f}_{X}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $…$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.25$ | $0.2$ | $…$ |
| $X=3$ | $0.05$ | $0.1$ | $…$ |
| ${f}_{Y}$ | $0.4$ | $0.6$ | $1$ |

Therefore, the probability mass function for  $Y$ is given by the following table:

| $y$ | $-2$ | $-1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.4$ | $0.6$ |

Finally, the  expected value of $Y$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}\,{f}_{Y}({y}_{i}) \\  & =(-2)\cdot 0.4+(-1)\cdot 0.6 \\  & =-0.8-0.6 \\  & =-1.4.\end{aligned}
$$
